status: source reviewed; awaiting art and local narration
reason: Original script names responsibilities but gives no sustained task that explains their consequences; abstract rails and tokens conceal the distinction.
teachingExample: Customer refund is an explicitly imagined task extending the source comparison of public-page reading and refund authority; no claim of a measured or real product demonstration.

evidence.quote: Policies should be local to the action boundary: reading a public page and issuing a refund do not require the same assurance.
The model may confuse this content with authorised instructions.
A memory entry should never gain authority merely because it was generated fluently or retrieved frequently.
The runtime can enforce schemas, rate limits, cost limits, data boundaries, and approval requirements.

artPlan.2: Public webpage and refund form share a customer request; read completes while payment remains awaiting approval.
artPlan.4: Retrieved quoted content attempts to enter trusted task memory; show provenance labels, then separate source text from actual user instructions.
artPlan.5: Close-up of the pending refund: typed arguments and a separate approval requirement; supporting information can progress without payment executing.

remainingReview: Six other scenes retain abstract art and need subsequent review; this targeted revision does not establish whole-film quality.
